chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Know that the beginning of the time is always superior, so hasten with goodness as much as you are able; and the most beloved of deeds to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is what the servant persists in doing, even if it be little.'

key_terms.أَوَّلُ الْوَقْتِ: The beginning/earliest time of a prescribed act, especially prayer
key_terms.مُدَاوَمَة: Constancy, perseverance, regular continuity in an act

ai.seo_question: Is it better to pray at the beginning of prayer time in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) conveys two foundational principles of worship to his companion Zurara: first, performing obligatory acts (especially prayer) at their earliest appointed time is always preferable; second, consistent regularity in deeds—even small ones—is more beloved to God than sporadic bursts of intensive worship. This teaching addressed the spiritual formation of the early Shia community, emphasizing that sustained devotion over quantity reflects true servitude to God.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Know, that the beginning time will always be superior, so hasten with the goodness whatever you are able to; and the most Beloved of the deeds to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is what the servant persists upon even though it be a little’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said

the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must note that the beginning of time always is better, so act faster for the good as much as you can. The most beloved of deeds in the sight of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, is that which a servant continues even if it is very little.’”
